desc: On 11 October 2017, seven days after Elizondo's resignation took effect and nine weeks before the New York Times story, To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science launched publicly with a live-streamed event and a Regulation A+ equity offering. The announced roster is the point: Tom DeLonge as President and CEO; Harold Puthoff as VP Science and Technology; Jim Semivan, recently retired from the CIA's clandestine service, as VP Operations; Steve Justice, 31 years at Lockheed's Skunk Works and latterly Program Director for Advanced Systems, as Aerospace Division Director; Luis Elizondo, described as former Director of Programs investigating unidentified aerial threats for the Office of the Secretary of Defense, as Director of Global Security & Special Programs; and Christopher Mellon, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Senate Intelligence Committee minority staff director, as National Security Affairs Advisor. Three divisions were announced: Science, Aerospace — explicitly including beamed energy and electrogravitics — and Entertainment. The timing means the corporate landing pad existed before the story broke.
